_doc: THE authoritative campaign configuration (2026-08-06 audit, section 5.5).
Sample sizes, block size, regimes, the E2 correlation and the secondary
fraction used to live as hard-coded constants in tools/run_campaign.py while
configs/experiments/screening.json sat next to them unread, so the file that
looked like the configuration was not the configuration. This file is read by
tools/run_campaign.py and its hash is stamped into every shard identity.
Adding a model to an existing campaign is forbidden: create a new campaign
entry instead, so an expanded panel can never be described retroactively as

notes: The pilot was a cost-measurement run, not an experiment. It executed E1 only,
for migliore_ca1 only, at 50 samples. The configuration previously declared
all eight models at 60 samples across three regimes, which gate D1 correctly
reported as 22 missing cells. Corrected to describe what was actually run.
Frozen discovery campaign. Sizes were set from the canonical-audit cost
measurements before any endpoint was computed.
mainen_l5pc and migliore_ca1 ran E1 only: at 256 draws their E2/E6 halves
(128 rows) fall below the 50-row floor build_ensembles needs for a regime to
be analysed at all, so simulating them would have produced no endpoint. This
was true of the stored campaign all along; the configuration now says so
instead of implying three regimes for every model.
Audit section 9.7: the expensive models cap every matched cell. Mainen and
Migliore yield only ~60-70 matched E7 points from 256 E1 draws, which puts
every model's E7 comparison below MIN_MATCH_N=120. Raising them to 512
accepted-eligible E1 draws is the minimum that lets an E7 half-subset clear
120. Written to its own shard namespace and merged by sample id, so the
frozen screening campaign is never mutated.

mainen_l5pc was REMOVED from this expansion. It is excluded from primary inference by gate N3, so enlarging its sample cannot improve any headline number; it accounted for 3.4 of the campaign's 3.7 hours. migliore_ca1 is retained because it is the BINDING constraint on the size-matched E7 cell (70 points against MIN_MATCH_N=120), and E7 is one of the two scored H-G direction criteria. Mainen sits at 76, so removing it does not lift the floor on its own -- only doubling Migliore does.

2026-08-08: `regimes` was declared as [E1] but the campaign executed E1+E2+E6 (E1 512 rows, E2 256, E6 256 = 1024 rows / 43 blocks, not the 512 / 21 the declaration implied). Gate D1 caught it. Root cause: build_jobs (tools/run_campaign.py:292) takes its regime list from the --regimes CLI argument, whose default is [E1,E2,E6], and consults only `regimes_by_model`; it never reads this campaign's top-level `regimes`. validate_campaign.py:92 does read it, so the two disagreed. `pilot` and `screening` were unaffected because their top-level list already was [E1,E2,E6] and they restrict per model. The declaration is corrected here to what actually ran rather than the data being discarded: the intended 512 E1 draws were produced exactly as designed, so the E7 expansion is unaffected, and the E2/E6 rows are additional valid simulations. Any future campaign that needs a restricted regime set must express it in `regimes_by_model`, not in the top-level `regimes`, until the runner is changed to honour the latter.
Audit R2 / priority 1 item 3: an independent scrambled Sobol design for the
same models, so campaign-to-campaign variation can be measured instead of
assumed. Same sizes as `screening` for the cheap models; the expensive ones
are sized for a usable E3 rather than for parity.

2026-08-08: `regimes` was declared as [E1] but the campaign executed E1+E2+E6 (762 blocks, not the 380 the declaration implied). Same cause as in screening_expand: build_jobs (tools/run_campaign.py:292) reads the --regimes CLI default [E1,E2,E6] and only `regimes_by_model`, never this campaign's top-level `regimes`, while validate_campaign.py:92 reads the config. Gate D1 caught the disagreement. The declaration is corrected to what ran. This is favourable here rather than merely tolerable: the scramble now covers the same three regimes as `screening`, so campaign-to-campaign variation can be compared across the full design instead of E1 alone, which is a broader test than the one originally specified.
External replication cohort (audit section 9.2/9.6 item 7). A NEW campaign
namespace, never an extension of `screening`. Sizes come from the measured
per-protocol cost in data/provenance/amplitude_calibration.json and from the
audit's >=256 accepted-E3 gate, subject to the workstation budget.

ortner_snc_da was fetched, adapted and audited but is NOT simulated: it fails gate N3 at every tested time step (ap_amplitude_mV on 1-2 of 7 prior points at 0.025, 0.0125 and 0.00625 ms) and its maximum rate of ~7.5 Hz gives <=3 spikes in the frozen 400 ms window. Two independent outcome-blind gate failures, decided before any information endpoint was computed.
moubarak_snc_da runs E1 only at 512 draws: its accepted setting is dt = 0.003125 ms (~49 s per sample), so E1+E2+E6 at 1024 would cost ~2.3 h of the budget for two secondary regimes.

tzilivaki_fsbc was fetched, adapted, its 53 mechanisms compiled, its f-I curve calibrated and its convergence audited -- and is NOT simulated. mean_firing_rate_Hz reproduces on 25-50% of audit points at dt = 0.05 and 0.025 ms on both the published 9,875-segment mesh and the 4,096-segment d_lambda mesh. A ~145 Hz fast-spiking cell needs a finer step than a 9,875-segment morphology allows within this budget. Gate N3 failure, decided before any information endpoint was computed for it.

miyasho_purkinje was fetched, adapted, its 20 mechanisms compiled, its f-I curve calibrated and its convergence audited over four time steps and two meshes -- and is NOT simulated. No setting converges, and the failing feature moves (ap_amplitude_mV at 0.05/0.025/0.0125 ms, membrane_tau_ms at 0.00625 ms), which points to threshold-adjacent prior samples rather than an under-resolved integration. Gate N3 failure.
